transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve been kind of planning my days around avoiding elevators. Like, I’ll take five flights of stairs at home, and I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I’ve also stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another option besides the elevator. It’s starting to affect what I do.
When you're in or near an elevator, do you feel sudden, intense fear or panic that feels like it peaks very quickly?

Yes. It comes on really fast. Like as soon as I start walking toward an elevator, or I hear it open, my chest tightens and my hands get sweaty. I get this rush of panic before I’ve even really thought about it.
Do you ever experience these sudden panic attacks in other situations, like in open spaces, crowded places, or when you're not near elevators?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed it happening in places like that. It seems tied to elevators, or when I think I might have to use one.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports sudden, intense fear and panic specifically tied to elevators, without similar episodes in other situations like open spaces or crowded places. This rules out panic disorder with agoraphobia (F40.009) and agoraphobia alone (F40.10), leaving specific phobia (elevator phobia) as the most likely diagnosis.

inference_history.note: The patient reports avoidance behavior centered around elevators, which introduces specific phobia (F40.290), agoraphobia (F40.009), and social anxiety disorder (F40.10) as candidates. Adjustment disorder (F43.22) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.2) are also considered due to the impact on daily functioning and potential ritualistic avoidance.
